author: rtehrani
text:
CISA adds exploited @SAPNews NetWeaver flaw to priority catalog

CISA has added CVE-2025-42884, an SAP NetWeaver vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog following evidence that attackers are exploiting the flaw in the wild. The agency added it on November 20, 2026, and set November 23, 2026, as the remediation deadline for federal civilian agencies.

That leaves agencies with a notably narrow response window. CISA’s current prioritization guidance calls for initial scoping within two hours of a KEV addition, reflecting a shift away from patch queues based mainly on severity scores. An actively exploited vulnerability generally warrants attention ahead of a similarly rated flaw for which there is no evidence of real-world abuse.

The issue involves improper neutralization of special elements in data-query logic within SAP NetWeaver. In practical terms, the weakness concerns how the affected software handles specially constructed input used in a query. CISA’s catalog entry establishes that exploitation has occurred, but it does not publicly answer every operational question, such as the identity of the attackers, the scale of exploitation, or their ultimate objectives.

KEV inclusion requires a CVE identifier, reliable evidence of exploitation, and an available remediation before CISA adds a flaw to the catalog. The entry therefore provides security leaders with a direct prioritization signal. It also points administrators toward the relevant SAP security update rather than leaving them with detection alone.

Exposure assessment should begin with an inventory of SAP NetWeaver and SAP Enterprise Portal deployments, including systems operated by business units, managed service providers, and acquired subsidiaries. Teams should identify externally reachable portals, determine their software and patch levels, and confirm whether network controls limit access. Internet exposure is particularly important because SAP Enterprise Portal can provide business-facing access to applications, information, and user sessions. https://t.co/yG2GpfUcJV

author: CVEStormSiren
text:
🟢 OVERBLOWN: Ghostscript (Upload2Shell)
CVE-2026-125396 · 8.5 v4
Real bug, real fix, but the "every upload box" hype outruns the risk.

Why it's overblown:
▪️ Not on CISA KEV; no in-the-wild exploitation reported
▪️ 8.5 v4 / 7.8 v3.1, local attack vector; EPSS 0.16%
▪️ Public PoC only proves memory control, runs no command; full RCE chains unpublished
▪️ Needs untrusted PS/EPS/PDF to reach Ghostscript (upload thumbnails, open CUPS queues)
▪️ Fixed in Ghostscript 10.08.0 since Sep 8

When to patch:
▪️ Routine: 10.08.0 or your distro fix in the normal cycle; rebuild containers
▪️ Sooner: within days if uploads, attachments or print jobs reach Ghostscript via Pillow, ImageMagick or CUPS
▪️ Urgent: now if a full exploit chain goes public or it lands on KEV

Real: researchers ran commands via Roundcube, WordPress plugin forms, MediaWiki and open CUPS in specific setups.

We'll post again if it hits CISA KEV or gets rescored higher.
#CVE #infosec

author: Follow_our_Echo
text:
🚨 Autonomous AI agents found a zero-day in MONAI Label and exploited it to run code as root on a university server.

According to Amazon Threat Intelligence, the attackers only gave the agents a list of targets and a goal. The agents did the rest:

→ They explored MONAI Label's API
→ About 11 minutes later, they were writing files outside its intended storage directory
→ In a later session, they turned that file write into RCE with the server's root privileges

All of this happened before defenders had a public advisory to act on.

The flaw: CVE-2026-133968, a critical path traversal (CVSS 9.8) in MONAI Label, an open-source tool for annotating medical images.

Authentication is off by default. In that configuration, anyone who can reach the server can exploit it without logging in.

What to do:
✅ Running 0.8.5 or earlier? Update to 0.8.6
✅ Restrict access from untrusted networks
✅ Enable authentication
✅ If an affected instance was exposed, check for signs of compromise

When agents find and weaponize bugs in minutes, how quickly you patch open source decides your exposure.

author: echelongraph
text:
A new Java flaw dropped this week with a name engineered to make CISOs flinch: "Java4Shell." It's a pre-auth remote-code-execution bug in OpenJDK. So — Log4Shell 2.0, all-hands, patch-at-2am?

Not quite. And the gap between the headline and the reality is the story.

What it is: CVE-2026-114938 is a memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder. When the decoder processes padded input (a stray =), hand-written x86-64 assembly miscalculates a store mask and writes past the end of the heap buffer. Feed Base64 to almost any Java app — a login form, a token, an upload — and you reach this code. That ubiquity is why it's scary.

Why it's narrower than the name suggests — the part that matters: 
🔹 It only triggers on OpenJDK 17.0.6+ running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 (VBMI). Java 8 and 11 don't have the intrinsic at all. Many servers (and most ARM/Graviton fleets) aren't affected. 
🔹 It's easy to crash, hard to weaponize. As of disclosure there was no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and no public working RCE exploit. One research team estimates under 0.12% of JVMs are actually at RCE risk. 
🔹 Severity itself is contested: 9.2 (CVSS 4.0, researchers) vs 8.1 (CVSS 3.1, Oracle).

So: real bug, worth patching — but "is it critical?" is the wrong question. The right one is "do we run an affected JDK, on an affected CPU, reachable with attacker-controlled Base64?" For most orgs the honest answer is "a small slice, not everything."

What to do this week: 
🔹 Patch to the fixed builds (17.0.21.1 / 21.0.13.1 / 25.0.5.1 / 27.0.1.1 — Oracle's Nov 2026 CPU). 
🔹 Inventory your JDKs: version ≥17.0.6 AND x86-64 AND AVX-512 is the exposure triangle. All three, or it's not RCE-exploitable. 
🔹 Prioritize internet-facing Java that decodes untrusted Base64 — reported examples include Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak in default configs. 
🔹 Short-term mitigation floated: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (disables the fast path). Unconfirmed by Oracle/OpenJDK — test before trusting it.

The lesson: a frightening nickname is not a severity score, and "ubiquitous + pre-auth RCE" is not the same as "exploitable in your environment." The teams that handled this well didn't panic-patch everything overnight — they answered where it actually applies in minutes, patched that first, and stayed calm about the rest. Signal over noise is a security capability.

🔎 Full breakdown of CVE-2026-114938 — affected builds, the AVX-512 condition, and fixes: https://t.co/029M9mNf8v
